doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Dream of Europe and moving abroad in 2000
summary: Miles Davis in Europe inspired him at twelve; he moved to Europe in September 2000 with a saxophone and three gigs, meeting Alvin Queen through Dr. Jesse Johnson.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I understand you spent a good deal of time in Europe, in fact in reading about you I believe it said you heard “Kind of Blue” in seventh grade and then you knew you wanted to go to Europe to play jazz?
So why? Why did you at that early age have this idea that Europe was going to be significant?

One of the records I got from the Columbia Record Club was “Miles Davis in Europe.” And you know I played it on my little hi-fi and you could hear how the music and the audience, the musicians and the audience just came together. They were somewhere in France because I remember the announcement was in French. And I just had that dream. That’s what I want to do. Yeah. And I was twelve. That’s what I wanted to do and I didn’t know how I was going to get it done but that was the goal, the dream. And so I moved over there in 2000. I made an exploratory trip over in the fall of 1999, and then I made another trip over in the spring of 2000. And I had some gigs over there anyway, I was working with another band and we were — I was working with the Spirit of Life

Ensemble at the time too, and we were doing things, mostly in France. But I was there, I went to Germany and Switzerland and I met different people and I was mapping out a plan. And I was back I think maybe a week and I got a phone call and I was invited to come and play some festivals with some folks in Switzerland in September. So that was in, I believe it was in May, end of May beginning of June I got the call. And the dates went in the book and that was it. So I left on September 20th, 2000. I had a saxophone, a suitcase and the promise of three gigs. And that was it man.
Yeah and from that I made my way. That was it man. I figured out how I was going to do it and that was it.
I wonder if you ran into Alvin Queen over in Switzerland.

Oh sure. But Alvin I had met some years earlier. One of my dearest friends and mentors Dr. Jesse Johnson I met Alvin through him. And Dr. Johnson gave me my first Mark VI back in — it’s a 1957 — yeah, my Mark VI. He said, “Look man, it’s time for me to pass this on because you’re going to take this further than I can go with it anymore. And I still have it. And her name is “Baby.” Yeah. But I met him through — I met Alvin through Dr. Johnson, I met Art Davis, the great bassist Art Davis, I met Stanley Cowell through him. Yeah.
